title: No web mutation waits on a row a reconcile pass holds
assertion: The web’s request pools and its queue producer’s pool set `lock_timeout` (three seconds) on every connection, a database URL cannot replace it, and the web’s own code opens a database connection no other way (the model gateway’s pool and the synthetic seed excepted, by name); while a second session holds a case’s row as a reconcile pass does, assigning the case answers `busy` with the closed word `records` after about the timeout and never after the holder, and writes no row, audit event or request key; with the row free the same assignment under the same request key goes through; a lock timeout outside the request’s transaction (the session’s row) or in a public handler is answered the same way, never as a server error, and a page’s is its error state, never “not found”; the same request key sent while its first request is still running is answered `busy` with the closed word `request`, and `duplicate` once the first has saved; a form’s words say what stays in it (what was typed, all but passwords and codes, or nothing on a form that is one button)
noFileReason: The reconciliation routes’ SYNTHETIC LED-06 practice on a pool opened as the web opens its own, with a second session holding a case’s row, a request key or the session’s row: no file.
